text:
Tomas Hertl is having the kind of season that makes a third-line role look like a waste of a good center. He's playing about 15 and a half minutes a night, yet Vegas takes 64% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he's out there, 14 points better than when he sits. That gap is one of the biggest on the team.

His nine goals match his chances almost exactly (9 on 8.8 expected), so nothing here looks borrowed. He has a six-game point streak, two-goal games against Pittsburgh and Buffalo, and ranks 43rd of 528 skaters in our wins added. The one oddity is that his minutes have dropped about a minute and a half over the last ten games while he produced more.

He'll be in the news for something else this week: Markerzone reported that his hit on Mavrik Bourque drew Ryan O'Reilly's anger and could draw a look from Player Safety. On the ice, Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking pegs him as a setup man who dumps the puck in more than he carries it, a forechecking center who still finds the shooter.
